analysis: I examined MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (head lines 529-1655) and the FlintResponseFormat.swift patch and base. Three changes were relevant. (1) Both ReasoningPromptProbe.streamingPrefix calls (lines 743 and 865) now pass modelType. This only affects parser seeding and has no data-exposure or authorization effect. (2) NativeToolStreamRouter now receives `streamedCalls: prepared` (line 1208). A new `router.streamsToolCalls` terminal branch (lines 1399-1431) handles `auto` tool calls that are emitted as deltas. That branch settles calls closed by a stop token via finishToolCalls, then runs checkNativeToolFailure, ToolConstraintValidation.validate and formatOutput.validate. Failures call releaseBox.fire() and finish the stream with an error, and success calls yieldTerminalInfo and releases. Usage and billing extraction through yieldTerminalInfo and usageSignal is unchanged. Cancellation and release behavior for the native-lease and media-drain paths is preserved, because this branch sits after the existing cancel and terminal checks. (3) FlintResponseFormatOutput.observe ignores .toolCallDelta, which is consistent with the Flint rule that response_format wins over tools. The residual-text path and the streaming path are both reachable only in `auto` mode. I identified no change to attestation, encryption, cache scoping (T-041 cacheScope and cacheEnabled plumbing untouched), consumer-lease handling, or the E2E boundary. Remaining uncertainty is outside the supplied evidence. NativeToolStreamRouter, `streamsToolCalls`, finishToolCalls and `prepared` as a streamedCalls argument are not visible, so I cannot confirm that per-frame validation covers unknown tool names and malformed arguments before deltas leave the provider. Tool-call content is model output sealed to the consumer, so I see no provider-side confidentiality regression. The streaming branch also skips the `tool_constraint_valid` telemetry emitted on the non-streaming path (the `requiresInferenceConstraint` block, lines 1471-1475), which is a minor observability difference with no security effect. A reviewer with the router source should confirm that validation failures after delta emission cannot be billed incorrectly or leave leases unreleased.
